title: arXiv Mathematics — 13 November 2026: 6 notable recent papers
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart. This is an inferred significance/cross-field selection, not a measured popularity ranking. The papers are new v1 submissions with too little citation history for meaningful momentum comparisons; the Semantic Scholar request was rate-limited, so citation metrics were not used.

sections.title: GFF for 3D Ising interfaces in three moves of Tetris
sections.abstract: The authors prove that, at sufficiently low temperature and positive interface slopes, the three-dimensional Ising interface has a Gaussian free field scaling limit, using mappings to SOS, half-monotone SOS and dimer surfaces.
sections.claimed_result: The authors' Theorem 1 proves local gradient convergence and convergence of centered rescaled height fields (modulo constants) to a linearly transformed GFF for the 3D Ising interface, SOS, HMSOS and bubble-free Ising interface.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Tilted tori with both limiting slopes positive; inverse temperature β ≥ β₀. The limiting amplitude and linear map depend on temperature and slope.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that extending the 3D Ising conclusion to every β > βc remains open; degenerate slopes such as (θ₁, 0) also remain unresolved, including the order of the positive-temperature height variance.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper states a scaling-limit theorem for four related surface/interface models and an improved renormalization result for interacting dimers; its probability and mathematical-physics cross-listing reflects the bridge in the work. Placement is based on scope and concreteness, not measured readership.

sections.title: The coercivity conjecture for nonlocal energies
sections.abstract: The authors show that uniform ellipticity alone does not ensure fractional Sobolev coercivity for broad classes of symmetric nonlocal kernels, while identifying cancellation conditions that recover coercivity and regularity in important cases.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.1 gives failure of a uniform H^s coercivity bound when n > 2s, including bounded discontinuous weak solutions. The paper also proves coercivity for specified kernel classes under extra cancellation/symmetry assumptions, and for n = 1, s > 1/2 under its stated hypotheses.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Symmetric measurable nonlocal kernels of order 2s, with 0 < s < 1 and the paper's uniform ellipticity/moment bounds. Positive results require additional structure or special kernel classes.
sections.unique_caveat: Uniform ellipticity is not enough in the counterexample regime; positive conclusions depend on the extra structure and hypotheses of the relevant theorems.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors give counterexamples to a named coercivity conjecture and a positive annular-cancellation criterion, with applications to variable stable kernels and non-cutoff Boltzmann kernels. This combines a sharp negative result with a structural positive theory; placement is significance-based, not an attention measure.

sections.title: A constructive computer-assisted existence proof for a Calabi--Yau metric
sections.abstract: The authors rigorously construct a Ricci-flat Kähler metric on the Fermat quartic using numerical approximation, a fixed-point argument and verified numerical bounds, and provide an explicit analytic approximation.
sections.claimed_result: The authors' Theorem 1.1 proves that a specified approximate Kähler form on the Fermat quartic can be corrected to a Calabi–Yau metric, with ‖u‖𝒳 ≤ 1.551 × 10⁻⁴ and ‖i∂∂̄u‖C⁰ ≤ 1.553 × 10⁻⁴ in the stated norms.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The certified construction concerns the Fermat quartic and the explicitly computed Kähler form/metric in the paper; verified bounds support the fixed-point argument.
sections.unique_caveat: The proof constructs this particular metric; adapting the rigorous numerical bounds and analysis to other manifolds remains a computational and mathematical task discussed by the authors.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A constructive, computer-assisted existence result in differential geometry with a high-energy-theory cross-list; Theorem 1.1 supplies explicit norm bounds for the correction to the computed metric. This unusual proof artifact supports inclusion, not popularity.

sections.title: Forbidden subset sums in a linear range: an inverse theorem and the Erdős-Graham irregularity problem
sections.abstract: The authors determine the extremal subset-sum function for c ≥ 1, prove multiple limit points for 0 < c < 1 (with an exact answer at c = 1/2), and establish an inverse theorem for dense sets with a prescribed subset sum.
sections.claimed_result: For c ≥ 1, f_c(n) = ⌊cn⌋ − ⌈n/2⌉; for 0 < c < 1, the authors prove limsup f_c(n)/n = c/2 and nonconvergence, with exactly {1/6, 1/4} as limit points when c = 1/2. Their inverse theorem says that, for q the least positive integer not dividing s, |A| ≥ E/q + εT forces a subset of A ⊆ {1,…,E} summing to sT for sufficiently large T and 2^(q−2)E ≤ sT.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: f_c(n) maximizes the size of a subset of {1,…,⌊cn⌋} avoiding n as a distinct-element subset sum. The inverse theorem has the stated size/range condition and sufficiently large T; only specified portions of the results are reported as Lean-formalized.
sections.unique_caveat: For general 0 < c < 1, the abstract gives multiple limit points and formulas along specified arithmetic subsequences, not every limit point for every c.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract reports explicit results on Erdős Problem #361 and an inverse theorem; selected results are machine-checked in Lean 4, and the paper is cross-listed in combinatorics and number theory. These are mathematical/formalization signals, not evidence of popularity.

sections.title: A counterexample to fixed-profile soliton resolution for the three-dimensional quintic wave equation
sections.abstract: For the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation, the authors construct a bounded global solution whose core approaches distinct stationary profiles along different limits, contradicting a fixed-profile soliton-resolution description.
sections.claimed_result: The authors construct a bounded forward-global solution asymptotic to a varying stationary profile plus one free wave; two limits of its core lie in distinct similarity orbits, ruling out the competing fixed-profile list described in the paper.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Three-dimensional focusing energy-critical (quintic) wave equation; the construction starts arbitrarily close to a particular sign-changing stationary state and uses a certified construction.
sections.unique_caveat: The result refutes the specified fixed-profile formulation through one constructed solution; it does not settle every broader or suitably generalized version of soliton resolution.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states a concrete counterexample to a fixed-profile formulation of a major asymptotic principle and reports a computer-assisted certificate for the stationary state and its complete odd energy kernel. It is a high-specificity result, though not cross-listed.

sections.title: Mass gap for the fractional $Φ^4_2$ model
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a stochastic-quantisation method for mass gaps in a high-temperature regime and apply it to prove exponential spatial-correlation decay for the fractional Φ⁴ model on the plane in the Wick-ordering regime.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish exponential decay of spatial correlations for the fractional Φ⁴ model on the plane in the Wick-ordering regime, using an auxiliary random walk to control propagation and dissipative estimates plus the Boué–Dupuis formula to control the renormalised nonlinearity.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Euclidean quantum field theory in a high-temperature regime; the application is the fractional Φ⁴ model on the plane in the Wick-ordering regime.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract's application is restricted to that model and regime and gives no quantitative parameter range or mass-gap result for all couplings or temperatures.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: This probability/mathematical-physics cross-listed paper gives a correlation-decay theorem and a proof strategy based on stochastic quantisation, perturbation propagation and a variational formula. Its placement follows the stated result and field bridge, not citation data.
